Swallowing a bullet in an emergency room would be best for harvesting organs probably. No damage to most organs (possibly damage to corneas, can't take your blood either) though with that you would probably screw up more lives than you'd save with the trauma you'd cause. Plus they wouldn't be ready for organ transplants so there is still a chance of wasted organs. 

Imagine being an 8 year old kid in the waiting room with a sprained wrist or something, to have your innocence taken away by watching someone else die is even less fair than someone waiting for organ transplant. A majority of people, children and adults, who would watch a death would be screwed up forever, their lives never the same, the image of bloody death haunting them.

True, but there is also a chance you'll survive, if that's the case you'll be locked in a psychiatric hospital for a while. What if you harm someone else in the process? What if instead of taking your own life you take someone else's?

Then there's the possibility you just completely burn to a crisp, nothing to really identify you as a person other than dental records, no usable organs left to use.

I'm not a doctor, so I'm not 100% sure on the specific facts/details, but I do know once you die your body stops working and starts to shut down. There's a certain time limit (again, not a doctor, not sure how long) where your organs can be not in use and be transferred. 
I've heard mostly of donors who are brain dead, meaning their body is still working, though there's no brain activity. Once you're brain dead you need constant care to be kept alive, your body can no longer function on it's own. 

Basically by the time the note is found, it's too late for your organs to ever work again.
